english: Let $f:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ be a differentiable increasing function with $f(2)=1$, and let $C$ be the curve $y=f(x)$. For every point $P(x,y)$ on $C$, the length of the subtangent at $P$ is equal to the radius of the circle that passes through the origin and $P$ and has its centre on the $x$-axis. If the point $(\alpha,6)$ lies on $C$, then the value of $\alpha^{2}$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $f:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ एक अवकलनीय वर्धमान फलन है जिसके लिए $f(2)=1$ है, तथा $C$ वक्र $y=f(x)$ है। $C$ के प्रत्येक बिन्दु $P(x,y)$ के लिए, $P$ पर अधःस्पर्शी (subtangent) की लम्बाई उस वृत्त की त्रिज्या के बराबर है जो मूलबिन्दु तथा $P$ से होकर जाता है और जिसका केन्द्र $x$-अक्ष पर है। यदि बिन्दु $(\alpha,6)$ वक्र $C$ पर स्थित है, तो $\alpha^{2}$ का मान ______ है।
solution: Circle with centre $(h,0)$ through $O$ and $P$: $h^{2}=(x-h)^{2}+y^{2}\Rightarrow h=\dfrac{x^{2}+y^{2}}{2x}$ (radius, as $x>0$).
solution_full: Let the circle through $O(0,0)$ and $P(x,y)$ have centre $(h,0)$. Equal radii: $h^{2}=(x-h)^{2}+y^{2}\Rightarrow 0=x^{2}-2hx+y^{2}\Rightarrow h=\dfrac{x^{2}+y^{2}}{2x}$. Since $x>0$, the radius is $\dfrac{x^{2}+y^{2}}{2x}$.

The subtangent at $P$ has length $\left|\dfrac{y}{y'}\right|$. Here $y=f(x)>0$ and $f$ is increasing, so $y'>0$ (where $y'$ would vanish the subtangent is undefined, which the condition excludes) and the length is $\dfrac{y}{y'}$.
Condition: $\dfrac{y}{y'}=\dfrac{x^{2}+y^{2}}{2x}$, i.e. $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{2xy}{x^{2}+y^{2}}$, a homogeneous differential equation.
Integrating: $\ln|v|-\ln|1-v|-\ln|1+v|=\ln x+c$, so $\dfrac{v}{1-v^{2}}=kx$ for a constant $k$, i.e. $\dfrac{xy}{x^{2}-y^{2}}=kx$, which gives $x^{2}-y^{2}=\dfrac{y}{k}$.
At $(2,1)$: $4-1=\dfrac1k\Rightarrow\dfrac1k=3$, so $C:\ x^{2}-y^{2}=3y$, i.e. $y=\dfrac{-3+\sqrt{9+4x^{2}}}{2}$, which is positive and increasing on $(0,\infty)$, as required.
originality_note: New: a curve defined by a geometric equality between its subtangent and the radius of the circle through O and P centred on the x-axis (way 5), which turns into the homogeneous equation y' = 2xy/(x^2+y^2) with a rectangular-hyperbola family. Closest known: curves with constant subtangent or subnormal; the differential equation of circles through O centred on the x-axis. Different because: the two objects are equated, giving a homogeneous DE whose solution needs a three-term partial fraction.
blueprint_concepts: Length of tangent, subtangent, normal and subnormal
Geometrical applications: tangent, normal, subtangent, subnormal conditions

concept_use.Length of tangent, subtangent, normal an: The subtangent length y/y' is the left side of the defining condition.
concept_use.Geometrical applications: tangent, norma: The geometric condition becomes y' = 2xy/(x^2+y^2), solved by y = vx with partial fractions to x^2 - y^2 = 3y.

stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol, curve and function introduced with its domain; conditions complete; one reading of each sentence; answer unique and equal to the plan (positive 2-digit integer); Hindi mirrors the English maths. Increasing and positive f makes the subtangent y/y' with one sign; DE solution unique through (2,1). No change.
key_step: Identify the radius (x^2+y^2)/(2x), form the homogeneous DE and integrate (1+v^2)/(v(1-v^2)) by partial fractions.
justification: Two ideas linked (geometric translation and a homogeneous DE needing a non-obvious partial fraction), more than the routine homogeneous DE 2025-P2-Q9 (L2) and level with the family-membership anchor 2021-P2-Q4 (L3).
